values.note: $20 a night at the first-come sites (grass pads, pay on site by QR code or cash envelope); $25 a night for the four online-reservable gravel-pad sites, plus a $4 processing fee per online reservation. Reservations are non-refundable.

values.note: 23 public campsites on the county's booking listing (sites 03-06 reservable with gravel pads, sites 01-02 and 07-23 first-come with grass pads), plus a camp host site; the park page counts 27 electric posts, some shared by two sites, and several tent areas.

values.note: May 1 to October 15, weather permitting; the campground may open earlier and stay open later, with water and the shower house shut off in cold weather and self-registration only (no online reservations) outside the season.

season.source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Butler/Park/Shell-Rock-Recreation-Area-and-Wildlife-Area/Facility/Shell-Rock-Site-03-Reservable/Availability (read 2026-11-04): 'Butler Campgrounds are open for camping May 1 through October 15 depending on weather conditions.'

values.note: Only sites 03-06 book online, up to a year ahead and at least 7 days ahead, with a two-night minimum on weekend reservations; an unreserved reservable site can be taken first come, paid online only. All other sites are first come, first served, held by placing a unit and paying at once. Check-in after 3 pm, check-out by 2 pm. After 14 nights campers must leave for 3 nights.

note: Butler County Conservation area on the west edge of Shell Rock, between the Shell Rock River and a fishing pond, with boat and canoe access, a prairie and a playground. The reservable sites have gravel pads; the first-come sites are on grass and some share an electric post with the next site. --Claude
summary: Rates confirmed ($20 first-come, $25 reservable + $4 online fee). Electric 30/50; water and sewer only at the host site, with a water fill station. 23 public sites + host (27 posts, shared). Showers, flush toilets, water. May 1 to Oct 15. Online booking for sites 03-06, the rest first come. Not waterfront stands: the loop is ~250-300 m from the Shell Rock River behind continuous forest, and the north water is a pond by the county's own word.
flags: WATERFRONT: 'not waterfront' stands. NAIP: the campground is a wooded loop west of the county road. The Shell Rock River (~45-60 m wide, imagery estimate; Overpass down) runs ~250-300 m east behind unbroken forest, with no view. North of the loop is an old-channel pond (~190 x 80 m of open water, about 3-4 acres, imagery estimate), ~60-100 m from the north end of the loop. The loop road and a lawn with a dock lie between, and the county calls it a pond ('Pond and River Fishing'). Under the 5-acre line, so no value. The stored evidence ('river backwater ~80 m NE') is this pond.
